faqs.a: Send your event date, the type of event, the location and roughly how many hours of coverage you need. Photographers can only confirm availability and give an accurate quote once they know the date and the length of the day.
faqs.q: What should I include when I contact a photographer?

faqs.a: Book as soon as your date and venue are fixed. Photographers usually cover a limited number of events per weekend, so popular dates fill first.
faqs.q: How far ahead should I book a photographer?

categories.intro: Event photographers capture the day as it happens: the people, the details and the moments you will want to look back on. Compare photographers by the events they cover, their packages and where they are based, then send an inquiry with your date.

faqs.a: Ask what you receive at the end (highlight film, full edit, social cuts), how long editing takes, and whether they need power or space at the venue for equipment.
faqs.q: What should I ask a videographer?

categories.intro: Videographers film your event and edit it into highlight reels, full-length films or short social clips. Use Eventory to find videographers by event type and location and ask what formats and turnaround they offer.

faqs.a: Most caterers price per guest. Your quote depends on the guest count, the menu, and whether you need buffet service, plated service or drop-off only. Include all three in your inquiry for an accurate figure.
faqs.q: How do caterers quote for an event?

faqs.q: Can caterers handle dietary requirements?

categories.intro: Caterers plan, cook and serve the food for your event, from drop-off trays to plated dinners with service staff. Compare caterers by their menus, service style and the events they cater, then send your guest count for a quote.

faqs.a: Your venue, event date, colour palette or theme, guest count and the setup and breakdown times allowed by the venue.

faqs.q: When should I book the venue?

categories.intro: Event venues range from banquet halls and hotel ballrooms to outdoor spaces and waterfront decks. Compare venues by capacity, the events they host and location, then check availability for your date.

faqs.a: Many do, but not all. Ask whether sound and lighting are included and how many guests or how large a space their setup covers.

faqs.q: How far ahead should I order a custom cake?

categories.intro: Florists create bouquets, centrepieces and floral installations for ceremonies, receptions and corporate events. Share your colours, venue and date to get a quote.

faqs.a: List the items and quantities you need, the event address, and the delivery and collection times. Delivery distance often affects the price.

categories.intro: Event planners and coordinators manage your event from planning to the day itself: timelines, vendors, budgets and on-the-day coordination. Find planners by the events they run.

events.intro: A wedding usually brings together more vendors than any other event: a venue, photographer, caterer, decor, florals, cake, makeup, entertainment and bar. Start with the vendors that take one event per day, then fill in the rest once your date is set.

events.intro: Corporate events such as launches, staff functions, award nights and family days need vendors who work to a brief and a timeline: venues, catering, audio-visual, photography, entertainment and planners.

events.intro: Christenings are usually smaller gatherings after the service, with catering, a cake, some decor and a photographer.

events.intro: A product launch needs a room, a way to capture it and something for guests to experience. Typical vendors are venues, video and photography, decor, a bar and a planner.

events.intro: Family days are daytime events for staff, members or communities. They usually need tents and rentals, catering, entertainment for children and adults, and decor.

events.intro: Religious events and celebrations often need a venue, catering suited to dietary customs, decor and florals.

events.intro: Fetes need a venue, sound and DJs, a bar, food and rentals such as tents, staging and barriers.
events.label: Fetes

events.intro: Conferences need a venue with the right capacity and layout, catering for breaks and meals, audio-visual support, photography or video, and often a planner.

events.intro: Graduation celebrations usually need a venue or rentals, catering, a cake, decor, photography and entertainment.

events.intro: Community events such as festivals and open days usually need rentals, sound and entertainment, food vendors and coordination.

events.intro: Private events such as anniversaries, dinners and house parties usually need catering, a bar, entertainment and decor.
